claims.content: To generate a random password and create a random keyfile for two factor authentication(password and keyfile) for the managed archives.

goal.raw_text: To generate a random password and create a random keyfile for two factor authentication(password and keyfile) for the managed archives.

claims.content: User
The user has selected the archive they wish to “lock” from the file manager interface.
The “Tools” menu is available and includes the “Create keyfile” command.
The Password and Keyfile generation utility dialog is displayed with a “Suggest password” control and a “Create keyfile” button.
The user selects “Create keyfile” from the “Tools” submenu after selecting the archive they wish to “lock” from the file manager interface.

trigger.raw_text: The user selects “Create keyfile” from the “Tools” submenu after selecting the archive they wish to “lock” from the file manager interface.

claims.content: The user selects the archive they wish to “lock” from the file manager interface.
The user presses the button writing “Tools”.
The user selects “Create keyfile” on the appearing submenu.
The user uses the button labeled “Suggest password” in the modal dialog box.
The user presses the button labeled “Create keyfile”.
The user sets the suggested password and optionally keyfile to the (created or updated) archive in one of the ways mentioned above.

Alternative from main flow step 0: during the archive creation process, the user presses the icon with the lock on it and sets password and (optionally) keyfile, according to user’s preference, to “lock” an archive.

Alternative from main flow step 2: for an archive to be updated that needs to be “locked”, the user selects the archive from the file manager interface, presses the button writing “Tools” on it, and selects “Enter password/keyfile” from the submenu; password and (optionally) keyfile may then be set in the window that appears.
Alternative from main flow step 2: the user presses F12 to create keyfile or random password instead of selecting “Create keyfile” from the “Tools” submenu.
PeaZip has generated a random password.
PeaZip has created a random keyfile.
The suggested password and (optionally) keyfile have been set to the (created or updated) archive.
The archive is encrypted (“locked”) by using a password and (optionally) a keyfile.
